{"edit_description":"CREATE A NEW FILE (does not exist yet): a single, fully self-contained HTML file `effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_zai-glm-5.3_01.html` — a realtime Gouraud-shaded rotating cube rendered with Canvas 2D ONLY (no WebGL, no external libraries, no network requests; must work opened directly via file://). Produce the complete working file per the spec below. All code comments in English.

== PAGE STRUCTURE ==
- `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<html lang="en">`, `<meta charset="utf-8">`, `<title>Gouraud-Shaded Rotating Cube — Canvas 2D</title>`.
- Dark page background (#0b0b12), canvas centered, internal resolution 800×600, CSS `max-width:96vw; max-height:92vh; image-rendering:auto`, subtle border.
- HUD as a DOM overlay div (position:absolute top-left over the canvas, monospace font): line 1 = "FPS: 61.2" (live), line 2 = "W — wireframe · P — pause" plus current mode status text like "[shading on]" / "[wireframe]" and "[running]" / "[paused]". Wrap canvas+HUD in a relatively-positioned container.

== 3D PIPELINE (all hand-written) ==
1. Cube geometry: 8 vertices at (±1,±1,±1). 6 faces (quads), each face = 4 vertex indices (consistent winding) + a distinct base RGB color (classic demo palette: red (216,64,64), green (64,192,96), blue (72,116,224), yellow (224,196,64), teal (64,200,196), magenta (192,80,200)). Each quad is split into 2 triangles → 12 triangles total.
2. Vertex normals for Gouraud: precompute once — for each of the 8 vertices, the normalized average of the 3 adjacent face normals (axis-aligned face normals), giving smooth per-vertex normals (each vertex normal is a unit (±1,±1,±1)/√3 direction). This produces the classic smooth Gouraud look while backface culling stays geometric.
3. Rotation: hand-written 3×3 rotation matrices Rx, Ry, Rz from angles; combined M = Rx·Ry·Rz. Per frame rotate all 8 vertex positions and all 8 vertex normals by M (matrix–vector multiply helpers, no matrix inversion needed).
4. Light: moving point light orbiting the cube: L(t) = (2.6·cos(lt), 2.1·sin(0.7·lt), 2.6·sin(lt)) with lt advancing over time. Optional ambient world light not needed.
5. Camera at (0,0,D) with D = 5.5 looking at origin along −Z. Perspective projection: depth = D − z_world (clamp depth ≥ 0.2); sx = 400 + f·x/depth; sy = 300 − f·y/depth (note the y flip), focal f = 600. These constants make the rotating cube (radius √3) fit within the canvas at all rotations.
6. Backface culling in SCREEN space (robust and doubles as degenerate-triangle guard): for each projected triangle compute signed area cross = (x1−x0)(y2−y0) − (x2−x0)(y1−y0); only rasterize triangles whose cross has the front-facing sign (pick the convention consistently — with the y-flip above and CCW world winding, front faces yield cross > 0; cull cross ≤ 0).

== PER-VERTEX LIGHTING (Lambert) ==
For each VISIBLE triangle (after culling), for each of its 3 vertices: lightDir = normalize(L − vWorld); intensity = ambient(0.16) + diffuse(0.84)·max(0, dot(vertexNormal, lightDir)) (vertexNormal already normalized after rotation). Vertex color = faceColor × intensity, each channel clamped 0..255. No specular (Lambert only, per request).

== GOURAUD SOFTWARE RASTERIZER (per-pixel interpolation, not canvas fills) ==
- One ImageData allocated once (800×600); wrap its buffer in a Uint32Array view for fast pixel writes; pixel packing little-endian: `(255<<24) | (b<<16) | (g<<8) | r`.
- Each frame: clear buffer with a precomputed dark vertical gradient (e.g. #10101c → #1a1a2a; per-row fill is fine).
- Triangle rasterization via edge functions / barycentric coordinates: clamp triangle bounding box to canvas; iterate pixels using pixel centers (x+0.5, y+0.5); weights w0 = edgeFn(v1,v2,p)/area, w1 = edgeFn(v2,v0,p)/area, w2 = edgeFn(v0,v1,p)/area; draw pixel only if all weights ≥ 0; color channels = w0·c0 + w1·c1 + w2·c2 (rounded), pack and write. NO z-buffer needed (cube is convex + culled).
- After all triangles: `ctx.putImageData(...)`.
- Then draw OVERLAY with the 2D context AFTER putImageData: the moving-light marker — project the light position with the same projection; if depth > 0 and on-canvas, draw a small glowing yellow dot (radial gradient, ~10px) so the orbiting light is visible; skip silently otherwise.

== WIREFRAME TOGGLE (key W, use e.code === 'KeyW') ==
When wireframe is ON: do NOT rasterize faces (buffer shows just the background gradient), and instead stroke the cube's 12 edges with ctx: edges belonging to at least one front-facing (visible) triangle → bright #e8e8ff, lineWidth 1.5; fully back-facing edges → dim rgba(200,200,255,0.22). Use projected vertex coordinates. When wireframe is OFF: normal Gouraud shaded rendering (optionally still stroke visible edges faintly on top — your choice, keep it subtle or skip). Toggle updates HUD status text.

== PAUSE (key P, e.code === 'KeyP') ==
Pause freezes animation state (rotation angles and light phase do not advance) but the render loop, FPS counter, and both key toggles keep working, so the HUD updates and you can still toggle wireframe while paused. Keydown handler should ignore e.repeat and call e.preventDefault() for these keys.

== FPS ==
requestAnimationFrame loop with timestamp parameter; dt = (t − last)/1000 clamped to ≤ 0.1. Count frames; every 500 ms compute fps = framesCount / elapsedSeconds and update the HUD text; keep a smoothed display. Rotation speeds approx: rx += 0.55·dt, ry += 0.9·dt, rz += 0.35·dt; light phase lt += 1.15·dt.

== CODE QUALITY ==
Organize into clearly commented sections (Geometry, Math, Pipeline, Rasterizer, Input, HUD, Main loop). Plain functions/consts, no classes needed. Keep it tight and correct — this must render correctly on first open. ~300-400 lines total.","path":"effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_zai-glm-5.3_01.html"}
